comparison: Both address the core AlphaFold predictions (C7-C12). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing they are computational models requiring experimental validation despite their testability. Peer reviewers rate them as SUPPORTED, affirming the models 'provide convincing evidence that leads to testable hypotheses' and can 'transform our understanding.' This represents a key disagreement on whether computational predictions alone constitute sufficient support.

Both address Smc1/Smc3 heterodimer structure predictions (C51-C57). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes validation by cryo-EM structures, while peer reviewers note consistency with published structures and accept the approach without objection. Strong agreement on this well-validated structural finding.

Both address the hinge's organizing role (C58-C64). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights systematic AF predictions with multiple constructs providing consistent evidence. Peer reviewers accept the structural insights and note the study 'serves as an example of how to use AF to build models.' Strong agreement.

Both address head engagement and joint junction mechanism (C65-C73). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic hypothesis about Scc1 NTD dissociation remains speculative despite circumstantial support. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, stating predictions 'suggest how formation of such a complex could stabilize an open state' and 'raise testable hypotheses.' Disagreement on whether the causal mechanism is sufficiently supported.

Partial overlap on genetic experiments (C79-C80). OpenEval R5 addresses C79-C87 (genetic experiments plus AF predictions) and rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing direct genetic demonstration combined with AF predictions. Peer R5 addresses C74-C80 (broader genetic context) and rates as SUPPORTED, noting consistency with published mutations. Both agree on support but cover slightly different claim sets.

OpenEval R5 addresses C79-C87 including both genetic experiments and AF predictions of Wapl/Pds5 motif interactions. Peer R6 addresses C81-C87 (only the AF predictions portion). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note models 'provide convincing evidence' and 'important insight into how Pds5 and Scc3/SA recruit different cofactors.' Agreement on the AF predictions component.

Both address Wapl-Pds5 interface predictions (C88-C92). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes how AF predictions explain phenotypes of existing mutations. Peer reviewers note 'remarkable congruence between cohesin subunit interfaces revealed by AF and the locations of mutations.' Strong agreement on this well-validated finding.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R7 addresses C93-C99 (ternary complex formation including motif effects) rated as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 addresses C93-C96 (subset focusing on conservation and E647) also rated as SUPPORTED. Both emphasize conservation across species and high confidence predictions. Agreement on the overlapping claims.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R7 addresses C93-C99 including the TYxxxR[T/S]ΦL motif effects (C97-C99). Peer R9 addresses only C97-C99 (motif comparison). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note this demonstrates 'the power of AF prediction methods.' Agreement on the motif analysis component.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R8 addresses C100-C109 (Scc1 NTD positioning and sequestration mechanism) rated as UNCERTAIN, noting AF does not spontaneously predict required unfolding. Peer R10 addresses C100-C103 (positioning only) rated as SUPPORTED. Disagreement stems from different claim scope: peer reviewers accept positioning predictions while OpenEval questions the full sequestration mechanism.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R8 addresses C100-C109 including conservation across species (C104-C107). Peer R11 addresses C104-C107 specifically (conservation and Rec8 extension) rated as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note this exemplifies 'how to use AF to build models of protein complexes.' Agreement on the conservation aspect, though OpenEval's broader evaluation is UNCERTAIN due to mechanistic uncertainties.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R8 addresses C100-C109 including mutation explanations (C108-C109). Peer R12 addresses C108-C109 specifically, rated as SUPPORTED, emphasizing 'remarkable congruence between cohesin subunit interfaces revealed by AF and the locations of mutations.' Agreement on explanatory power of mutations, though OpenEval's overall evaluation of the broader mechanism is UNCERTAIN.

Both address Scc3-Smc3 interface and acetylation protection (C110-C112). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes how AF predictions explain mutations and suppressor mutations, providing validation. Peer reviewers note results 'provide important insight into how Eco1 and Sororin antagonize Wapl' and explain 'how acetylation blocks releasing activity in yeast.' Strong agreement.

Both address Eco1 recruitment and binding (C113-C116). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights consistency with crystal structure and coherent mechanistic model. Peer reviewers note results 'provide important insight into how Esco acetyl transferases are recruited to Smc3 by Pds5.' Strong agreement on this structurally validated finding.

Both address Ctf4-Mcm7 interaction (C117). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with prior co-IP and crosslinking data. Peer reviewers accept the prediction as consistent with the overall AF-based approach. Strong agreement on this finding informed by prior experimental data.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R12 addresses C118-C124 (Sororin binding and competition mechanisms) rated as SUPPORTED. Peer R16 addresses C118-C122 (Sororin binding specificity) also rated as SUPPORTED. Both emphasize conservation across species and specificity for Smc3. Agreement on the overlapping binding predictions.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R12 addresses C118-C124 including Wapl competition (C123-C124). Peer R17 addresses C123-C124 specifically, rated as SUPPORTED, noting 'mutually exclusive binding provides clear mechanistic explanation.' Agreement on the competition mechanism component.

Both address Scc2/Nipbl-Scc3/SA interactions (C125-C127). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes partial validation by cryo-EM for one interaction and novel prediction for the second. Peer reviewers accept both predictions without challenge. Strong agreement, though OpenEval notes the functional significance of the nose interaction requires further investigation.

Both address established background knowledge (C1-C5, C13-C50). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are well-supported by cited literature and provide essential context. Peer reviewers accept this established knowledge without challenge. Strong agreement that these represent background rather than novel findings. Minor difference: Peer R19 includes C6 which OpenEval R14 does not explicitly list.
